items.title: LLMs reward expertise
items.author: MaxMussio
items.summary: Expertise enhances LLM performance; domain knowledge improves prompt effectiveness. Reinforcement learning models integrate human preferences into LLM training. Effective reward design is crucial for LLMs to perform complex tasks.

items.title: Amazonian civilization had estimated 3M people in 3% of forest area
items.author: marojejian
items.summary: An ancient civilization in the Amazon rainforest had an estimated population of 1.25 to 3 million people, occupying less than 3% of the area around the first millennium. This civilization built large ceremonial earthworks, but its collapse remains unexplained. The Amazon was likely home to tens of millions before European colonization.

items.title: Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science
items.author: milkshakes
items.summary: An internal model solved ten major open problems in mathematics and theoretical computer science, including high-dimensional sphere packing and a disproof of the Erdős unit-distance conjecture. These breakthroughs span various fields like geometry, coding theory, and group theory.

items.title: Windows XP 2002 for the Itanium: Unbridled rage
items.author: jandeboevrie
items.summary: Windows XP 2002 for Itanium was an early 64-bit version, but Microsoft later discontinued support for Itanium in favor of x64 processors. Emulation of Itanium with QEMU allowed running Windows XP on Itanium. Microsoft focused on x64 for mainstream markets.

items.title: There Will Come Soft Rains (1950) [pdf]
items.author: pmg101
items.summary: "There Will Come Soft Rains" is a 1950 science fiction short story by Ray Bradbury about a house in an obliterated city. The house remains until destroyed by fire. The title references a Sara Teasdale poem.

items.title: Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code
items.author: mpweiher
items.summary: Manually retyping LLM-generated code helps prevent cognitive debt by improving understanding and reducing reliance on the machine. This method allows for deeper comprehension and better code quality. It's a slower but more effective way to work.

items.title: Launch HN: Hoplite (YC S26) – Effortlessly deploy cloud coding agents
items.author: BenceRed
items.text:
Hi HN, we’re Bence and Ryan, founders of Hoplite (https://hoplite.sh). Hoplite lets you deploy coding agents in the cloud, with a suite of tools that makes it incredibly easy to QA features. During onboarding, we port over your local setup - sessions, memories, MCP servers, and get your projects ready to run in the cloud.

Here’s a demo: https://youtu.be/bnykt
items.summary: Hoplite is a cloud coding platform that simplifies deploying local development environments in the cloud. It was launched by Y Combinator-backed founders. The service aims to eliminate issues with local development setups.

items.title: Frame selection is the whole game: notes on making LLMs watch video
items.author: cortexosmain
items.summary: Frame selection in LLMs for video understanding uses algorithms to pick key frames, improving efficiency and accuracy. This method reduces computational load while maintaining relevant context. It enhances performance on video question answering benchmarks.

items.title: Bonsai: Janestreet's UI Library
items.author: KolmogorovComp
items.summary: Bonsai is an OCaml library for building interactive web UIs, inspired by Elm, used by Jane Street for all their web applications. It separates state management from rendering. It allows functional composition of UI components.

items.title: AirLLM 70B inference with single 4GB GPU
items.author: Anon84
items.summary: AirLLM enables running 70B-parameter models on a 4GB GPU without quantization, using layer-by-layer loading. It trades speed for memory efficiency. It's an open-source solution.

items.title: Twenty Years of Pandoc
items.author: fiddlosopher
items.summary: Pandoc, released in 2006, has become a popular document converter supporting over fifty formats. It has been updated over two hundred times and is now integrated into academic tools. Pandoc 3.9 supports WASM for browser use.

items.title: What's the largest software project AI can complete on its own?
items.author: yusufozkan
items.summary: AI can autonomously complete large projects like reimplementing a bioinformatics toolkit with 16,000 lines of code. The most complex software AI has independently developed is a C compiler. AI's potential in software development is vast and transformative.

items.title: LLMs Can't Jump
items.author: gmays
items.summary: Large Language Models lack the ability to make the abductive leap needed for true scientific invention, as they can't ground their reasoning in physical reality. They excel at induction but not abduction. This limits their potential for groundbreaking discoveries.

items.title: Qwen3.8-Max: A New Bar for Coding and Cowork
items.author: ai2027
items.summary: Qwen3.8-Max is a highly advanced model with 2.4 trillion parameters, set to release its open weights next week, excelling in autonomous coding and cowork tasks.

items.title: SQLite Critical CVEs or LLM Slop?
items.author: ymir_e
items.summary: Recent CVEs for SQLite were likely fabricated, citing non-existent functions and unrelated code. None appear in official SQLite advisories. NVD rated them high despite lack of proof.

items.title: The Shape of Things to Come, Part 2: Model Welfare for Agentic Engineers
items.author: networked
items.summary: Agentic engineers now focus on orchestration and oversight, using AI agents to execute code, while emphasizing automated verification and model benchmarking. Custom agents are prioritized for efficiency. Agentic development shifts workflows to rely on AI-driven execution.

items.title: Show HN: Product analytics (and evals) for agent sessions on your MCP
items.author: screm
items.text:
Hi HN! We’re Theodore and Louis, founders of Armature (YC P26). We reconstruct the entire session behind the MCP tool calls you receive, including what the user asked their agent to do and what the agent thought.

You wrap your MCP in 3 lines of code (our SDK is available in Typescript, Python and Go) and start seeing in your dashboard: - All sessions reconstructed: it’s like reading the real conversation the user had inside Claude or ChatGPT! - A ranking of your MCP most popular use cases, bui
items.summary: Armature offers product analytics for agent sessions on your MCP, capturing user interactions and agent responses. It integrates easily and doesn't change your server. It provides insights into functional effectiveness, reasoning quality, and trustworthy output.

items.title: What DMARC Protects You From, and What It Does Not
items.author: adulion
items.summary: DMARC protects against domain spoofing and phishing but does not secure inbound emails from external sources. It verifies emails from your domain but does not prevent attacks on other domains.

items.title: The Potomac River Midair Collision
items.author: mplanchard
items.summary: On January 29, 2025, a midair collision occurred over the Potomac River involving a PSA Airlines jet and a U.S. Army helicopter, killing all 67 people on board. The NTSB found systemic failures by FAA and Army in route management and safety oversight. The collision was the deadliest U.S. air disaster in over two decades.

items.title: DDoS against Norwegian government IT infrastructure – status
items.author: e12e
items.summary: In June 2022, Norway faced a DDoS attack affecting multiple government ministries, with no lasting impact reported. The attack's origin and extent remain unknown. Norwegian authorities are taking the incident seriously.

items.title: The AI Productivity Gap
items.author: kiyanwang
items.summary: The AI productivity gap highlights uneven AI adoption, with top users saving more time but many losing gains to rework. AI's potential benefits are not fully realized due to skill and workflow mismatches. Efforts to bridge this gap are crucial for equitable productivity gains.

items.title: Show HN: Nightcrawler – A local AI pentesting agent running on a smartphone
items.author: NickySlicks
items.summary: Nightcrawler is a local AI pentesting agent running on smartphones, designed to perform reconnaissance without cloud resources. It leverages local processing and offloaded services to minimize battery and data usage. The project was showcased on Hacker News.

items.title: Kraid is a now a real compiler
items.author: losgehts
items.summary: Kraid is a new compiler for the Panfrost driver stack that now passes all Vulkan CTS compute shader tests, marking it as a fully functional compiler. It is designed to replace the outdated compiler in the stack.
